utterances.speaker: Council Staff

chapters.summary: Chair Sanchez greets attendees, identifies herself as chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings, and announces votes on Intros 717-A and 1023-A. She describes 717-A as requiring DOB to inform property owners about permit sign-off and 1023-A as authorizing electronic HPD registration and fee payment.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez opens vote on Intros 717-A and 1023-A

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: You are muted, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Piedadina Sanchez, Chair of the Committee on Housing and Buildings.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Today, the committee will be voting on proposed intros number 717A in relation to requiring the Department of Buildings to inform property owners of permits and offer...

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Requirements and proposed intro number 1023A in relation to authorizing electronic development and electronic payment of the fee associated with such registration.

chapters.summary: Sanchez recounts a joint oversight hearing on homeownership and says buying a home is hard, but holding onto one is becoming just as difficult. She cites rising property taxes, insurance, utilities, and repair costs and argues city bureaucracy should not add to the burden.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez frames bills as relief for homeowners facing rising costs

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: On Tuesday at our joint oversight hearing with the Finance Committee on advancing and protecting homeownership, we heard a message loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Buying a home in New York City is hard enough, but for many New Yorkers, holding on to one is becoming just as difficult.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Rising property taxes, insurance, utilities, repair costs are putting enormous pressure on homeowners, many of whom have worked their entire lives to build that stability for their families.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The last thing they need is city bureaucracy adding to that burden, which is why today we are voting on two bills that represent practical steps that we can take.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: to make the city processes simpler, clearer, less burdensome for property owners.

chapters.summary: Sanchez explains DOB's role in reviewing construction plans and issuing permits, noting average permit approval time has risen to about 23 days. She describes how open permits can block title transfer, delay property sales, and force owners to undo work for inspection.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez explains DOB permit process and open-permit risks

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The Department of Buildings is tasked with the examination of construction plans to ensure compliance with New York City construction codes and the issuance of work permits upon the approval of such plans.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Over the last three years, the average number of days from the filing of an application for a permit to the approval of such applications has increased to about 23 days.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Where opening a permit gives the department notice that construction or renovation work has commenced, closing a permit informs the OAB that the work is complete.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: At the conclusion of the project, the approved work is to be inspected to ensure compliance with both the submitted and approved construction plans and the New York City construction codes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And if necessary, a new or amended certificate of occupancy is issued by the department.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: After a project is completed, the owner of the property or the representative must ensure that reports for all required special inspections are submitted,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: city inspections are performed, self-certifications of labor completed by contractors of record, and a final inspection is performed.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Partly to confirm that the owner has completed these tasks,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Department of Buildings requires that the owner or the representative signs off on the completion of the permit.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: When permits are left open because owners have failed to sign off on the completion of a project, owners can discover that they are unable to transfer title, delaying the sale of their property, and may even need to undo complicated

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: work for the sake of allowing inspection, further amplifying the costs.

chapters.summary: Sanchez says owners of properties with two or more units, or non-owner-occupied homes, must register annually with HPD. She notes the online form still must be printed, hand-signed, and mailed, causing delay and paper waste, and says the bills aim to streamline these processes.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez describes HPD paper registration burden and bill goals

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Separately, every year, owners of properties with two or more housing units or owners of any residential property not occupied by the owner of the family must register these properties with the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, HPD.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And while HPD offers an online system to complete property registration forms, the completed form it produces must be printed, hand-signed, and physically mailed to HPD.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This physical signature requirement causes delay for property owners, produces paper waste, and a lot of things are lost.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This is news headline.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: New York City is not yet run by AI.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The bills voted on today aim to streamline these processes through educating property owners and bringing property registration completely online.

chapters.summary: Sanchez explains Intro 717-A, sponsored by Council Member Salaam, would require DOB to notify owners with open permits that sign-off is required. DOB would email an initial notice within seven days, send follow-ups after permit expiration, and post resource guides on its website.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez details Intro 717-A permit sign-off notification requirements

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Intro 717A.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: By Councilmember Salam would require the Department of Buildings to notify property owners with open permits that the permits must receive DOB sign-off.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: DOB would be required to email an initial notice within seven days of the issuance of a permit, with such notice informing property owners of the consequences of failing to obtain sign-off alongside instructions for accessing DOB's online self-service portal.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This bill would require the Department of Buildings to send follow-up notifications two months after the expiration of a permit and six months after the expiration of a permit if such a permit has not been renewed and yet to receive sign-off within 30 days of expiration.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, this bill would also require the Department of Buildings to send follow-up notifications two months after the expiration of a permit and six months after the expiration of a permit if such a permit has not been renewed and yet to receive sign-off within 30 days of expiration.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Department of Buildings to develop a resource guide on sign-off requirements with such guides posted to the department's website.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, this bill would also require the Department of Buildings to send follow-up notifications two months after the expiration of a permit and six months after the expiration of a permit if such a permit has not been renewed and yet to receive sign-off within 30 days of expiration.

chapters.summary: Sanchez says Intro 1023-A, sponsored by Council Member Banks, would let property owners register with HPD electronically. Electronic signatures would be sufficient, HPD would maintain the online system, and owners could pay the filing fee electronically.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: 1023A by Councilmember Banks would give property owners that need to register their property with HPD the option of doing so through an electronic registration system.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, this bill would also require the Department of Buildings to send follow-up notifications two months after the expiration of a permit and six months after the expiration of a permit if such a permit has not been renewed and yet to receive sign-off within 30 days of expiration.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Electronic signatures obtained via this method would be deemed sufficient for registration purposes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: HPD would be required to maintain the electronic registration system on its website and to accept electronic payments of the filing fee through such a system.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Finally, this bill would also require the Department of Buildings to send follow-up notifications two months after the expiration of a permit and six months after the expiration of a permit if such a permit has not been renewed and yet to receive sign-off within 30 days of expiration.

chapters.summary: Banks says he introduced Intro 1023 to modernize property registration by allowing owners to complete annual registration electronically. He notes owners can currently access forms online but must still print, sign, mail, and sometimes use a separate fee system.
chapters.title: Banks says Intro 1023 modernizes HPD registration from print-and-mail

utterances.text: I introduced this legislation to modernize New York City's property registration process by allowing property owners to complete their annual registration electronically.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: This is a simple common sense reform.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks

summary: The Committee on Housing and Buildings voted on Intros 717-A and 1023-A, both adopted 11-0-0.
Intro 717-A, sponsored by Council Member Salaam, requires DOB to notify property owners about permit sign-off requirements and consequences of open permits.
Intro 1023-A, sponsored by Council Member Banks, authorizes electronic HPD property registration and electronic payment of the associated fee.
